cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles, far from home (Ezekiel 1:1-3). In the sixth year, he's sitting in his house with the elders of Judah sitting before him. And right there, in the middle of company, the hand of the Lord GOD falls on him.
Ezekiel looks and sees a figure like that of a man. From His waist down, His appearance is like fire, and from His waist up, He's as bright as the gleam of amber.
He stretches out what looked like a hand and takes Ezekiel by the hair of his head. The HAIR, friend, and with a mustache this size, I felt that one all the way down to my gold base.

cards.question: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up between earth and heaven and carries him in visions of God to ___.
Ezekiel ends up at the entrance of the north gate of the inner court. What's there?
There in Jerusalem, Ezekiel sees something just like the vision he saw back in the plain. What is it?

answers.text: The glory of the God of Israel

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to lift his eyes to the north, and there's that idol of jealousy again. Then God asks if he sees what the house of Israel is doing. God says these great abominations are driving Him far from His sanctuary.
After asking Ezekiel if he sees these abominations, what does God tell Ezekiel he will still see?

answers.text: The people turning back to Him

cards.text: Next, God brings Ezekiel to the entrance to the court, and Ezekiel spots a hole in the wall. It's just a hole, friend, and I'm ALREADY nervous.

cards.question: At the hole in the wall, God tells Ezekiel to leave the wall alone and just peek through the hole.

cards.text: So Ezekiel digs through the wall and finds a doorway. It's like pulling the couch out to vacuum, except what's back there is WORSE.

God tells him to go in and see the wicked abominations they're committing there. Ezekiel looks, and engraved all around the wall is every kind of crawling creature and detestable beast, along with all the idols of the house of Israel.

cards.question: Inside that hidden room, who's standing in front of all those engravings?

cards.text: Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stands among them, and each man has a censer in his hand, with a fragrant cloud of incense rising. Seventy grown men in a secret room behind a wall, and they made sure it SMELLS nice.

cards.question: The elders are doing this in the darkness, each at the shrine of his own idol. They're saying the LORD does not see them.

cards.text: They also say the LORD has forsaken the land. Meanwhile, God is right there giving Ezekiel a guided tour of the room, so yeah, fellas, He sees you.

Again, God tells Ezekiel he'll see them committing even greater abominations, and friend, this tour has more levels than a parking garage. Then He brings Ezekiel to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD.

cards.question: At the north gate of the house of the LORD, Ezekiel sees ___ sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.

cards.text: God asks him, "do you see this?" and says there are even greater abominations than these. Then He brings Ezekiel into the inner court, to the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar.

cards.question: About twenty-five men are standing between the portico and the altar. They're facing the temple of the LORD.
With their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, what are these twenty-five men bowing to in worship?

cards.text: Backs to the house of the LORD, bowing to the sun. That's like turning your back on your boss on payday... so you can go thank the ATM.
God asks Ezekiel, "do you see this?" Then He asks if the abominations they're practicing here aren't enough for the house of Judah.

cards.question: God asks if the abominations in the temple aren't enough for the house of Judah. Where else does He say they're doing wrong?

answers.text: Down in the land of Egypt

cards.text: They fill the land with violence and keep provoking Him to anger. And then one more: "Look, they are even putting the branch to their nose!"

cards.question: After everything God has shown Ezekiel, how does God say He will respond?
God says that although they shout loudly in His ears, He will listen to them.

cards.text: So Ezekiel stands there with all of it in front of him. Hold on tight, friend, because this vision is still going.

findings.problem: The statement being judged also uses Ezekiel 8:5: God tells Ezekiel to lift his eyes north, and he sees the idol of jealousy. Citing only 8:6 leaves part of the statement without its reference. The card should cite Ezekiel 8:5-6, or the verse 5 setup should be moved to an earlier story card.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: "Inside that hidden room" and "all those engravings" point back to cards 11-12, which are no longer on screen. The question also never names Ezekiel or freshly establishes the scene, so it is not self-contained.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the already-answered facts that the men have their backs to the LORD's house and are bowing to the sun, then adds the ATM joke. It introduces no new moment or detail from the vision, making it a recap card rather than a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
